title: Tomorrow, Maybe
tagline: A speculative sketch of everyday life, extrapolated from today's trends.

locale.persona: an imagined household in a mid-sized U.S. city

morningRoutine.activity: Wake on a light sleep cycle
morningRoutine.detail: A sleep tracker picks the lightest moment within your wake window, and the room lights brighten slowly like a sunrise.
A personal assistant summarises overnight messages, flags what needs a decision and drafts replies for you to approve.
Alongside familiar food, plant-based and fermentation-made dairy and meat could be ordinary supermarket items.
Rooftop solar, a home battery and a heat pump balance themselves against grid prices before you are awake.
An autonomous electric shuttle for office days, or mixed-reality meetings from home for the rest.

places.title: The front page
places.description: There may be no single front page. News could arrive as a personal feed, summarised by AI, with provenance labels showing where each claim and image came from.
places.imageAlt: A translucent holographic news feed with summary cards and verification badges
highlights: Every story carries a verified-source label
AI summaries at three reading depths
Heat-wave and flood alerts by neighbourhood
Live translation of every outlet in the world

places.title: The bedroom
places.description: Adaptive lighting and cooling, lightweight AR glasses on the nightstand instead of a phone, and very few visible screens.
places.imageAlt: A minimal bedroom with soft glowing walls and a pair of AR glasses on the nightstand
highlights: AR glasses replace the phone on the nightstand
Walls that glow to a sunrise schedule
Quiet heat-pump cooling for hotter summers
Sleep data shared only if you allow it

places.title: The street
places.description: Fewer parked cars, more trees and shade, autonomous shuttles, delivery robots on the pavement and quiet electric everything.
places.imageAlt: A leafy street with an autonomous pod shuttle, a delivery robot and cyclists
highlights: Former parking lanes turned into trees and bike lanes
Street lighting that dims when nobody is around

technology.name: AR glasses
technology.description: Glasses that overlay directions, captions and video calls on the world, possibly replacing the smartphone screen.

technology.name: Personal AI agent
technology.description: An assistant that books, buys, writes and negotiates on your behalf, within limits you set.

technology.name: General-purpose home robot
technology.description: A robot that can fold laundry, load the dishwasher and tidy up, the long-promised robot maid finally useful.

technology.name: Autonomous electric vehicles
technology.description: Shared driverless pods that you summon rather than own, charging themselves overnight.

technology.name: Brain–computer interfaces
technology.description: Implants and headsets that restore movement and speech today could become wider-use controllers, if they prove safe.

technology.name: Holographic entertainment
technology.description: Volumetric video lets you watch a concert or match as if from any seat in the venue.

futureVisions.whoSaidIt: Space agencies and private launch companies

futureVisions.prediction: Atmospheric carbon finally falling, with damaged ecosystems recovering.
Healthy lifespans of 100 years becoming ordinary.
A three-day working week, with AI doing most routine work.
futureVisions.whoSaidIt: Economists, echoing Keynes a century earlier

headlines.headline: Grid runs on clean power for a full year
First crewed mission returns from a Mars base rotation
Cities replace a third of parking lanes with trees

sceneCaption: A speculative holographic projector, rendering a wireframe Earth.
